statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-111997 (GHSA-rxp7-6hxx-x8q5): ip-address up to 10.7.3 matches an Address6 zone identifier in quadratic time before checking its length, so one long string with many % characters can stall the process. It is fixed in ip-address 10.7.4, which finds the zone by index instead of with a regular expression. Sources: https://github.com/beaugunderson/ip-address/security/advisories/GHSA-rxp7-6hxx-x8q5, https://github.com/beaugunderson/ip-address/commit/ec80fcd5d7b97defecfd39717d782a9f9f8b89dd, https://github.com/beaugunderson/ip-address/releases/tag/v10.7.4. We read the bundled package.json files in every published npm package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository, x86_64 and aarch64 (11.8.0-r0 to 11.21.3-r0), each checked against the index checksum, together with the npm-doc and npm-bash-completion subpackages built from the same source, which contain no copy of ip-address. Each npm build bundles one copy of ip-address, under /usr/lib/node_modules/npm/node_modules/ip-address, the same on both architectures. ip-address is 10.1.0 to 10.7.1 in every build from 11.8.0-r0 to 11.21.2-r1, inside the affected range, and 10.7.5 in 11.21.2-r2 and 11.21.3-r0. The shipped dist/ipv6.js agrees in every build: up to 11.21.2-r1 it still finds the zone with the regular expression, and from 11.21.2-r2 it finds the zone by index as the fix does. The range ends at 11.21.2-r2.
